status.description: active = ready for delivery; archived = soft-deleted via PATCH status:archived (excluded from list by default); expired = past 90-day TTL. Note: pending/failed statuses belong on segments, not audiences.

quote_id.description: ID of the most recent delivery quote for this audience.

quote_total_cents.description: Total cost in cents from the most recent delivery quote.

parent_audience_id.description: ID of the audience this was forked from (null if not a fork).

forked_from_snapshot_version.description: Snapshot version of the parent audience at the time of forking.

record_count.description: Total resolved records across all composed segments.

matched_record_count.description: Records contributed by matched-subtype segments in this audience's composition. Present only when the composition includes at least one included matched segment; null for pure-filter or non-matched compositions.

match_count.description: Records resolved to a known identity, for an audience created via the direct file-upload flow (POST /v1/match/file). Populated when that upload's matching pipeline completes; null before then or for audiences not created that way — use matched_record_count for a composition-level matched count instead.

input_record_count.description: Rows in the originally uploaded identity file, for an audience created via POST /v1/match/file. Same population conditions as match_count.

match_rate.description: match_count / input_record_count, rounded to 4 decimal places. Null unless both match_count and input_record_count are present.

expires_at.description: ISO date — 90-day hard expiry from creation

visibility.description: org (default) — visible to all members of the org. private — visible only to the creating user.

segment_refs.description: Composition of segments that define this audience. Each entry specifies a segment and its role (include or exclude) in the set operation.

role.description: Whether the segment's records are included in or excluded from the audience.

segment_ids.description: Cache of include-role segment IDs (denormalized from segment_refs for query efficiency).

excluded_segment_ids.description: Cache of exclude-role segment IDs (denormalized from segment_refs for query efficiency).

segments.description: Expanded summaries of the include-role segments, in `segment_ids` order. Populated on both list and single-GET responses. Best-effort — missing or deleted segment docs are skipped, so this array may be shorter than `segment_ids`.

excluded_segments.description: Expanded summaries of the exclude-role segments, in `excluded_segment_ids` order. Same expansion semantics as `segments`.

set_logic.description: How the include-role segments are combined: `union` = a record matches ANY included segment (OR); `intersection` = a record must match EVERY included segment (AND). Segments in `excluded_segment_ids` are always subtracted from that result (AND NOT), regardless of `set_logic`.

campaign_id.description: The one campaign this audience belongs to, or null.

EnrichmentRelease.description: Delivered IAG refresh version. Independent of license status. Null provenance means unknown; a newer refresh-major can prompt a refresh through existing workflows. Active licenses and existing identity IDs support free refresh; normal charges may apply otherwise.

ExpandedSegment.description: Constituent segment summary and saved filter definition. Audiences may combine multiple segment subtypes; there is no primary segment or audience subtype.

record_count.description: Cached record count of the segment. Null if never counted.

input_record_count.description: matched subtype only. Count of records in the uploaded identity file. Null otherwise.

match_count.description: matched subtype only. Count of records successfully matched. Null otherwise.

Filter.description: A single filter condition for audience discovery or job execution

field.description: Canonical catalog field_name (e.g. age or state). ZIP5 also accepts zip, zip_code, or postal_code as input aliases; saved responses use zip5.

text_comparison.description: Optional STRING comparison mode for =, !=, IN, NOT IN, and LIKE, or ARRAY<STRING> membership mode for ARRAY_CONTAINS and ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY. Defaults to exact. Case-insensitive mode applies Unicode case folding to both the stored value and the supplied value.

trim_whitespace.description: Optionally trim leading and trailing whitespace on both sides of a STRING or ARRAY<STRING> comparison. Defaults to false; independent of text_comparison.

value.description: The value to match against. For state, a published two-letter code or full State name is accepted and normalized to the code. Scalar types (`string`, `number`, `boolean`) are used for single-value operators (`=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `LIKE`, `ARRAY_CONTAINS`). Pass an **array** for `IN`, `NOT IN`, and `ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY` — pass the array directly with no comma-encoding. `BETWEEN` takes a two-element array `[low, high]`. Omit entirely for `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` checks.

FilterGroup.description:
A group of Filter conditions. All `filters` within a single group are **always ANDed together** — there is no per-group intra-operator. The `combinator` attribute is an **inter-group** operator: it controls how this group is joined to the immediately preceding group in the array. The `combinator` on the first group (index 0) is always ignored.

Example — `(city = "NYC" AND state = "NY") OR (state = "CA")`:
```json [
  { "id": "g1", "filters": [{"field":"city","op":"=","value":"NYC"},
                            {"field":"state","op":"=","value":"NY"}],
    "combinator": "AND" },
  { "id": "g2", "filters": [{"field":"state","op":"=","value":"CA"}],
    "combinator": "OR" }
] ```
Group g1's `combinator` is irrelevant (it is the first group). Group g2's `combinator: "OR"` means the result is `(g1) OR (g2)`.

id.description: Stable identifier (UUID or NanoID). Used to track groups across edits.

filters.description: One or more filter conditions. All conditions in this array are combined with AND. Provide at least one filter per group.

combinator.description: **Inter-group operator.** Joins this group to the previous group in the array. `AND` narrows the result; `OR` broadens it. Ignored on the first group (index 0) — that group has no predecessor to join.
